# Introduction

{{< include _subfiles/logistic-regression/_sec_overview_bernoulli_models.qmd >}}

::: notes
This chapter assumes familiarity with
the measures of association for [binary outcomes](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/data.html#def-binary-var) —
risks, [risk differences](binary-outcome-associations.qmd#def-RD) and ratios, [odds](binary-outcome-associations.qmd#def-odds), [odds ratios](binary-outcome-associations.qmd#def-OR),
and the [logit](binary-outcome-associations.qmd#def-logit-fn) and [expit](binary-outcome-associations.qmd#def-expit) functions —
which are reviewed in
[Measures of Association for Binary Outcomes](binary-outcome-associations.qmd).
:::

# Introduction to logistic regression

::: {.callout-tip title="Video lecture"}
David Rocke's Epi 204 lecture
[*Introduction to Logistic Regression*](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/EPI204-2021-03-30.mp4)
([slides](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/EPI204-1%20Introduction%20to%20Logistic%20Regression.pdf))
continues from [risks and odds ratios](binary-outcome-associations.qmd)
to generalized linear models, the [logit](binary-outcome-associations.qmd#def-logit-fn) link,
and fitting and interpreting [logistic regression models](#def-logistic-regression) in R
[@rocke2021epi204].
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Video tutorial"}
Josh Starmer's StatQuest video
[*StatQuest: Logistic Regression*](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yIYKR4sgzI8)
gives a visual overview of logistic regression:
modeling the probability of a [binary outcome](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/data.html#def-binary-var),
and fitting the model by [maximum likelihood](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-mle) rather than least squares
[@starmer-statquest].
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Video lecture"}
Richard McElreath's
[*Modeling Events*](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RuBUVQELw-c)
(Statistical Rethinking 2026, Lecture A09)
accompanies Chapters 10 and 11 of @statrethink2e,
which cover generalized linear models for binary and count outcomes.
The lecture fits these models using Bayesian inference
rather than the maximum likelihood estimation used in this chapter
[@mcelreath2026rethinking].
:::

# Understanding logistic regression models

::: {.callout-tip title="Video tutorial"}
Josh Starmer's StatQuest video
[*Logistic Regression Details Pt1: Coefficients*](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vN5cNN2-HWE)
explains how [logistic regression](#def-logistic-regression) coefficients are interpreted on the [log-odds](binary-outcome-associations.qmd#def-logodds) scale,
for both continuous and [categorical predictors](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/data.html#def-categorical-var)
[@starmer-statquest].
:::

# Estimating logistic regression models

::: {.callout-tip title="Video lecture"}
David Rocke's Epi 204 lecture
[*Logistic Regression and Likelihood*](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/EPI204-2021-04-01.mp4)
([slides](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/EPI204-2%20Logistic%20Regression%20and%20Likelihood.pdf))
covers [maximum likelihood estimation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-mle) for [logistic regression](#def-logistic-regression),
deviance,
and comparing models with [AIC](Linear-models-overview.qmd#def-aic) and [deviance tests](#def-deviance-test)
[@rocke2021epi204].
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Video tutorial"}
Josh Starmer's StatQuest video
[*Maximum Likelihood, clearly explained!!!*](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XepXtl9YKwc)
introduces the idea of maximum likelihood estimation
[@starmer-statquest].
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Video tutorial"}
Josh Starmer's StatQuest video
[*Logistic Regression Details Pt 2: Maximum Likelihood*](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BfKanl1aSG0)
shows how maximum likelihood estimation fits a logistic regression curve
[@starmer-statquest].
:::

{{< include _subfiles/logistic-regression/_sec_logistic-fitting.qmd >}}

# Inference for logistic regression models

::: {.callout-tip title="Video lecture"}
David Rocke's Epi 204 lecture
[*Inference for Logistic Regression*](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/EPI204-2021-04-06.mp4)
([slides](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/EPI204-3%20Inference%20for%20Logistic%20Regression.pdf))
covers [likelihood ratio tests](#def-lrt) for nested models,
[Wald tests](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-wald-test) and [confidence intervals](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/inference.html#def-confidence-interval),
and interaction terms,
using the Evans County heart disease data
[@rocke2021epi204].
:::

# Model comparisons for logistic models {#sec-gof}

::: {.callout-tip title="Video lecture"}
David Rocke's Epi 204 lecture
[*Diagnostics and Goodness of Fit*](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/EPI204-2021-04-13.mp4)
([slides](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/Lecture5_Diagnostics_Logistic_Regression.pdf))
covers the [deviance goodness-of-fit test](#def-deviance-test)
and the [Hosmer-Lemeshow test](#def-hosmer-lemeshow)
[@rocke2021epi204].
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Video tutorial"}
Josh Starmer's StatQuest video
[*Saturated Models and Deviance*](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9T0wlKdew6I)
explains saturated models, null deviance, and residual deviance
[@starmer-statquest].
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Video tutorial"}
Josh Starmer's StatQuest video
[*Logistic Regression Details Pt 3: R-squared and p-value*](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xxFYro8QuXA)
explains a likelihood-based pseudo-$R^2$ for [logistic regression](#def-logistic-regression)
and the [likelihood ratio test](#def-lrt) of the fitted model against the intercept-only model
[@starmer-statquest].
:::

{{< include _subfiles/logistic-regression/_sec_logistic_gof.qmd >}}

# Residual-based diagnostics

::: {.callout-tip title="Video lecture"}
David Rocke's Epi 204 lecture
[*Diagnostics and Goodness of Fit*](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/EPI204-2021-04-13.mp4)
([slides](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/Lecture5_Diagnostics_Logistic_Regression.pdf))
covers residuals, [leverage](#def-leverage-glm), and influence diagnostics
for grouped and ungrouped logistic models,
and [overdispersion](count-regression.qmd#def-overdispersion)
[@rocke2021epi204].
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Video tutorial"}
Josh Starmer's StatQuest video
[*Deviance Residuals*](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JC56jS2gVUE)
explains how [deviance residuals](#def-deviance-residual-logistic) are computed and used
[@starmer-statquest].
:::
